newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FULL TEXT-BHP statement on steel business.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT-BHP statement on steel business.

text.p: The following is a full text of an announcement by The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd on the futures of the company's steel business.
BHP STEEL - BLUE PRINT FOR THE 21ST CENTURY
The Broken Hill Proprietary Company Limited (BHP) today announced the outcomes of the strategic review of its world wide steel operations.

Executive General Manager and Chief Executive Officer BHP Steel, Mr R J (Ron) McNeilly, said the review had confirmed that the world steel industry would continue to be characterised by intense competition, falling prices, increasingly demanding customer needs, the emergence of new low capital intensive technologies and the need for a relentless focus on cost reduction.
"BHP is determined to meet these challenges, ensure the viability of its steel business and deliver the level of returns that our shareholders expect," Mr McNeilly said.

"A reshaped Australian business with a strong focus on value-added downstream businesses supplying the building and construction markets of the Pacific Rim will position our steel business for the future."
The major conclusions reached involve:
- Restructuring BHP Steel before the end of the decade to meet the Company's return on capital requirements in the 21st century, consistent with our commitment to safety and the environment;
- Greater focus on anticipating and meeting the expectations of our markets by building skills, organisations and plant facilities that are competitive and deliver what our customers want;
- Addressing issues such as sub-scale operations, plant and product complexity and technology to improve cost competitiveness and provide a better service to our customers;
- Developing the ability to respond to global opportunities and create opportunities for new partnerships;

- Improving capital efficiency and plant effectiveness and eliminating duplication of facilities; Reducing the exposure to unprofitable exports; Reducing overheads and eliminating over-management and the duplication of functions.
The following specific decisions will be implemented:

- The strategic review has confirmed and endorsed the Steel Group's multi domestic growth strategy, which is focussed on servicing the building and construction markets in the Pacific Rim. This strategy will continue to be pursued and will involve the further establishment of high added value coated products facilities together with further downstream processing and
merchandising facilities;
- Involvement in relevant downstream businesses of a significant scale will continue. Further opportunities for growth in the Pacific Rim will be pursued in line with the multi domestic strategy;

- Steelmaking at the Newcastle plant will be phased out by the end of 1999. However, the existing bar and rod mills will form the nucleus of a world class rod, bar and wire business with these facilities at Newcastle expanded;

- Feed for the Newcastle Mills will be produced at the Sydney Steel Mill and Whyalla Steelworks. The development of facilities at Whyalla to produce the required Newcastle feed will proceed immediately, and they are expected to be operating in 1999;
- Geelong Rod Mill will close during 1999 with rod production being centred at Newcastle;
- Sydney Wire Mill will close during 1999 and further wire manufacturing capacity will be installed at Newcastle which will become the centre of the Company's wire business;
- By the end of 1999 export business from Australasian plants will focus on added value flat products;

- Port Kembla Steelworks will continue its development as a flat products integrated steelworks with capacity rounded out to 5 million tonnes per annum. by 1999. Further development of these facilities will be aimed at achieving world scale in each of its main activities;

- Whyalla Steelworks will continue to operate at its current capacity of 1.2 million tonnes per annum supplying structurals and rails to the Australian market together with billets for the Newcastle Rolling Mills;
- Organisationally BHP Steel will be restructured around four businesses: Integrated Steel Division, Coated Steel Division; Rod, Bar and Wire Division and Building and Industrial Products Division;
-Steel Group headquarters will remain in Melbourne. It will be substantially restructured and downsized with a focus on strategy and policy formulation;
- The four businesses will take full responsibility for their activities including international operations and growth, and consequently the existing International Division will be disbanded;
The Steel Group's executive team will comprise the following:
Mr R J (Ron) McNeilly, Executive General Manager and Chief Executive Officer BHP Steel
Mr G A (George) Edgar Group General Manager and Chief Operating Officer Integrated Steel Division (Port Kembla)
Dr R L (Bob) Every Group General Manager and Chief Operating Officer Coated Steel Division (Sydney)
Mr R W (Bob) Kirkby Group General Manager and Chief Operating Officer Rod, Bar and Wire Division (Newcastle)
Mr G M (Grahame) Parker Group General Manager and Chief Operating Officer Building & Industrial Products Division (Sydney)
Mr D R (Roger) Zimmerman Group General Manager Finance (Melbourne)
Mr G S (Garry) Evans Group General Manager Human Resources and External Affairs (Melbourne)

"The new structure will give the businesses total responsibility for the production and marketing of their products and shift the focus of our resources closer to customers and markets," Mr McNeilly said.
"The combined integrated steel business will deliver the benefits of scale and specialisation in supplying feed to support our downstream businesses".

Mr McNeilly said he recognised that the implementation of a number of these decisions would present difficulties, but overall they provided a foundation for reshaping the future of the Steel Group in a very competitive environment.

"I especially regret the need to close steelmaking at Newcastle," he said. "Newcastle was the Company's entry point to steelmaking and the foundation from which we have built our presence in the industry.
"Major industries have been built around this base and a great many people have contributed to the Works whilst also adding to the Newcastle community and its lifestyle".

Mr McNeilly paid tribute to these efforts and reaffirmed the Company would retain its presence in Newcastle and would build a world class rod, bar and wire industry around existing and new facilities at that centre.
"In Whyalla, whilst the steelmaking facilities are sub-scale, we have the unique advantage of being close to high quality iron ore reserves," he said.

"This enables Whyalla operations to be sustained, and its importance to our Steel business will be enhanced by both the decision to provide steel to Newcastle and by other initiatives to improve costs and capital efficiency at that centre. Notwithstanding this, the Whyalla facilities will remain under intense competitive pressure and the replacement of the existing facilities at the end of their useful working life cannot be automatically assumed.

"Our New Zealand operations are also sub-scale and our business there is under increasing pressure from deteriorating domestic market demand, depressed international steel prices and a strong New Zealand dollar. In addition, New Zealand Steel's steelmaking facilities are based on a relatively complex technology.

"While we have significantly enhanced the plant's potential by doubling productivity in the last five years and investing in new metal coating facilities it is difficult to envisage the replacement of the plant's steelmaking facilities at the end of their current life, estimated to be no more than 10 years.
Indeed, should business conditions not improve, it is entirely possible that the steelmaking facilities will close earlier.

"The major capital expenditure requirements of our existing businesses are now largely behind us. We expect to contain our expenditure on these assets to considerably less than depreciation charges, resulting in a significant reduction in the capital base over time.

"BHP Steel sees its greatest opportunities for world competitiveness and growth in the flat products segment of the steel industry. We see our major integrated steelmaking and hot strip rolling activities in Australasia being increasingly

centred at Port Kembla. Such a plant configuration, together with the decisions reached in regard to the rod, bar and wire business will deliver products more competitively and enhance our performance.

"The way forward is to continue to pursue our multi-domestic growth in Asia, reduce our exposure to low profit exports, drive down our costs and reconfigure our steelmaking and rolling facilities to best advantage.
"We believe this strategy will deliver the most sustainable outcomes for our shareholders, customers, employees and the communities in which we operate.

"The international steel industry has many challenges. There are also exciting opportunities to enhance profitability and growth. We are determined to ensure BHP remains a leading-edge steel company that will create wealth for our stakeholders."
